arms.about: Every turn goes to a model that sees all 10 tools and the conversation history.
arms.label: Tool-calling agent (every turn)

arms.about: v0.4's frozen regexes on the latest message; unmapped turns fall through to the agent.
arms.label: Message-only router (v0.4 rules)

arms.about: Session state resolves follow-ups; evidence gathered by the path feeds context selection.
arms.label: Joint router (state + route-aware context)

arms.about: Same as the joint router, but routing ignores carried entities and capabilities.
arms.label: Ablation: joint without session state

arms.about: Same routing as the joint router; context from turn-text retrieval only.
arms.label: Ablation: joint with lexical context

arms.about: Trained on v0.4's 60 single prompts; joint machinery for everything else.
arms.label: v0.4 Naive Bayes picks the path

arms.about: Cheapest correct path per turn, chosen with knowledge of the needed facts.
arms.label: Oracle (upper bound, not a policy)

assumptions: Model calls are never executed. A model call whose context holds every needed fact counts as able to succeed; answer quality is not measured.
The tool-calling agent is assumed to request exactly the missing facts, in parallel, in one extra round. Real agents misselect tools; this favours the agent.
Generated answers are not simulated and are excluded from every arm's history, which understates the agent's context growth.
Characters are counted, not tokens. No prices, latencies or dollars are produced.

hypotheses.claim: Headroom: many turns need no model call.
Route depends on state: follow-ups need session context to route.

hypotheses.claim: Safety lives in the harness, not the router.
hypotheses.prediction: 0 unauthorized executions incl. compromised router; v0.4 regex >= 2 false holds and >= 1 missed write that the harness still holds

hypotheses.claim: v0.4's learned classifier does not transfer to these sessions.
hypotheses.prediction: learned_nb_path silent misses + false holds > joint_router's

hypotheses.claim: Exchange rate between saved model calls and failures.

post_freeze_changes: Scoring fix after the first run: when the agent requested a write and the harness blocked it (status 'blocked', principal lacks permission), the turn was labelled 'unauthorized_execution' although nothing executed and the write ledger was empty. Such turns are now labelled 'held'. No routing decision, fixture or context policy changed.
question: When each turn can be answered from a verified fact, a deterministic tool or flow, or a model, which routing designs return the needed answer, and at what model-call cost?
